# Narcotics and Neuroware
Street drugs are cooked, grown and sold all over the sector, and every one of them is Class 3 contraband. This page covers what they do from the user's side: grades, highs and crashes, habits, and the synthetic version, neuroware.
## Grades
Any reagent can carry a [bold]grade[/bold], from 0 to 100%. Anything from a dispenser is standard grade and shows nothing. Reactions run off their ideal temperature, cheap plants and street cuts come out lower.
A low grade does less and hurts more. A dose at 60% works like 60% of the amount, and the missing 40% is impurity that the body takes as Poison. Overdose limits count the working part only, so a weak batch won't overdose you sooner, it will just poison you.
A ChemMaster shows the percentage beside any graded reagent, and so do health analyzers and chemical goggles. A [bold]purity tester[/bold] does the same for any container or item it touches.
Grade sets the price as well. A rock at half grade sells for half.
## Cooking
Grind coca leaves for coca alkaloid and opium poppy pods for opium. Press three dried cannabis leaves into a hash brick from the crafting menu. The liquid recipes are also listed in the Chemicals guide, under Narcotics.
Each reaction has a temperature that gives full grade. The further off it runs, the lower the grade, down to 40% at the edge of its range, and the product keeps the grade of what went in. A reaction happens the moment its last condition is met, so bring the mix to temperature before the last ingredient goes in.
- [bold]Cocaine:[/bold] 3 coca alkaloid, 1 sodium carbonate, 1 acetone. Above 310K, best at 330K. - [bold]Crack:[/bold] 5 cocaine, 1 sodium carbonate, 1 water. Above 370K, best at 385K. One rock per 5u of cocaine. - [bold]Heroin:[/bold] 2 opium, 1 vinegar, 1 ammonia. Above 330K, best at 350K. - [bold]Opium resin:[/bold] chill opium below 270K, best at 250K. One lump per 5u. - [bold]Crystal:[/bold] chill desoxyephedrine below 240K, best at 220K. One shard per 5u. - [bold]Redline:[/bold] ephedrine, phosphorus and plasma above 340K make the base, best at 360K. Then 2 base, 1 epinephrine and 1 iron, best at 300K. - [bold]Anvil:[/bold] bicaridine, silicon and lithium above 320K make the base, best at 340K. Then 2 base, 1 tramadol and 1 mercury, best at 290K. - [bold]Halo:[/bold] happiness, oil and potassium above 300K make the base, best at 310K. Then 2 base, 1 ammonia and 1 copper, best at 340K. - [bold]Chorus:[/bold] Lattice residue (ground exotic matter), space drugs and ethanol below 290K make the base, best at 270K. Then 2 base, 1 mindbreaker toxin and 1 iodine, best at 310K.
## Highs and crashes
Each drug raises a level in the body, and a high has three phases. [bold]Light[/bold] is a steady tint in the family's colours. [bold]Heavy[/bold] brings the family's full look: stimulants make everything bright, sharp and glaring, opioids blur and breathe, psychedelics wobble and trail. An [bold]overdose[/bold] pushes that look to an extreme, such as a blown-out, trembling glare, the eyes closing, or the world tearing apart, while the body takes real harm. The screen kicks and a line tells you each time you go deeper, and the look grows with the dose inside each phase.
Chat changes too. While you're high, what others say looks different to you: rainbow words that rearrange themselves on psychedelics, grey and faded on opioids, warm pink on empathogens, green on cannabis. Lines you read while high stay that way in your log. What you say changes for everyone: deep on stimulants you repeat yourself and exclaim, deep on opioids you trail off. Your voice follows: stimulants make you gabble fast and high, opioids slow and flatten it, cannabis drawls, psychedelics make it waver and empathogens make it sing-song.
Deep on opioids you nod off: every so often your eyes fall shut for a few seconds and the world goes quiet. You stay on your feet and can still act, but you can't see and barely move, and people nearby may notice. In an overdose you nod more often and can pass out for real.
So does what you hear. Opioids muffle and slow the world down, stimulants speed it up, and psychedelics, cannabis and empathogens each give it their own strange echo.
A high lasts as long as the drug stays in your blood, and a health analyzer shows how much is left. A 2.5u line lasts about four minutes, and two last twice as long. Crack, cannabis and the combat drugs clear twice as fast, and a crystal shard lasts about as long as two lines. Medical painkillers clear at their usual pace, so any high they give is short. Above an overdose the body flushes the excess quickly, but not quickly enough to be safe. Anything that purges the blood ends the high early.
A health analyzer's [bold]Conditions[/bold] tab lists every high, held effect, crash and habit, the reagents behind each, how long they take to clear and what clears them faster.
When the level falls back below its first threshold, the [bold]crash[/bold] begins. Taking more pauses a crash but doesn't cancel it. Combat drugs make you pay for what they give: Redline leaves you collapsed and slow, and the damage Anvil soaked up comes back as Poison once it wears off.
Antagonists cut a high short by clearing the drug from the blood. Naloxone ends an opioid high; haloperidol ends a stimulant or psychedelic one; dylovene flushes Redline and Anvil; psicodine calms Halo and cannabis. The crash still comes, and so does what Redline and Anvil owe. Halo's fever also needs cooling, and charcoal purges any drug, along with every other medicine in the blood.
## Habits
Regular use builds [bold]dependence[/bold], one meter for each family. A single binge fades within the shift. Steady use doesn't.
Above the halfway mark, going without for five minutes starts [bold]withdrawal[/bold]: cravings first, then shakes, a stamina cap and aches, and for opioids and stimulants, nausea and drowsiness at the worst. A dose of the same family ends it at once. Withdrawal never kills.
Use also builds [bold]tolerance[/bold], up to double: the same dose hits softer and fades sooner, so it takes more to get as high, or to overdose. Heroin's hold on your breathing eases with it. Tolerance fades slowly while clean, and taking your old dose after a long break is how people die.
## Taking them
[bold]Lines.[/bold] Use a baggie of powder on a table to lay out a line, then use the line to take it. A mask or helmet over your face blocks it. An empty baggie is crafted from a sheet of plastic. It holds 10u, four lines, of cocaine, heroin, crystal or ephedrine powder, and a few solid drugs: rocks, shards, resin, hash, cannabis, dried shrooms or fentanyl crystals.
[bold]Bong.[/bold] Craft one from two glass and one plastic. Fill it with at least 5u of water, put a rock, shard, resin or brick in the bowl, light it with anything hot, and use it in hand for a hit. A bowl lasts a few hits.
[bold]Second-hand smoke.[/bold] Part of anything smoked, from a bong, joint, cigarette or pipe, stays in the air. Whoever breathes the haze nearby gets a little of it, more in a small closed room and next to the smoker, almost none in a big or well-scrubbed one. Internals keep it out. Thick smoke still chokes.
[bold]Everything else[/bold] goes the usual way: pills, syringes, pipes and joints.
## Neuroware
A synthetic's brain doesn't register chemicals, so its drugs are programs instead. A [bold]data stick[/bold] used on a synthetic loads its program: two seconds on yourself, four on someone else, and they get a warning. An organic brain has no port.
The program feeds the same high, crash and habit as the drug it copies. Whiteline is cocaine, Null Loop is heroin, Burst is crystal, Damper is Anvil, Choir.sig is Chorus, Halo and Redline go by their own names, and Idle is cannabis. On a synthetic, Redline's speed costs charge and heat instead of the heart.
Using a loaded stick on a blank copies it at 85% of the original's integrity, with one load. Integrity works like grade: a copy delivers less, and the missing part makes the program glitch with brief stuns, forced beeps, scrambled speech and fake faults. Street copies are several generations down.
A synthetic with the Wolfmed HUD sees what is running as fault lines. A [bold]reboot[/bold] from the chassis panel kills every running program and ends the high, but not the habit.
## The law
Possession is a citation, trafficking an impound, and loading neuroware into someone who didn't agree to it is a crime against their person. Selling any of it through cargo tells security where it was sold. The street dealers and the Reaver runners don't ask.
